Field observations confirm that nest attentiveness remains high throughout this period, with females maintaining egg temperatures near the optimal developmental range.

The timing of puberty appears to be influenced by local food availability, with individuals from more productive habitats achieving maturity earlier than those from resource-limited sites. This developmental flexibility may buffer the population against interannual variation in environmental conditions.
